event_54d70037980fae4d.title: Manatee Tempest activity group
event_54d70037980fae4d.description:
The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport

event_0874d586fa054456.title: System recovery setting tampering
event_0874d586fa054456.description:
System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set default recoveryenabled no]

Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

This detection might indicate that the malware was stopped from delivering its payload. However, it is prudent to check the machine for signs of infection.

event_bd32012bd37197a2.title: Suspicious service launched
event_bd32012bd37197a2.description: A suspicious service was started on this device. Attackers might use services to launch malicious commands or programs. This technique is used to maintain persistence or elevate privileges on the target device.

event_d5ea42b15d70abe4.title: Suspected overpass-the-hash attack (Kerberos)
event_d5ea42b15d70abe4.description: Emma Clark (Helpdesk Administrator) on VNEVADO-Win10V attempted to authenticate against VNEVADO-DC.

event_2552bcec96d217c2.title: Suspected DCSync attack (replication of directory services)
event_2552bcec96d217c2.description: Julian Burke (IT director) on VNEVADO-Win10V sent 1 replication request to VNEVADO-DC.

mapping.value: Suspected DCSync attack (replication of directory services)

event_4923ae609ccf8698.title: Suspicious sequence of exploration activities
event_4923ae609ccf8698.description: A process called a set of windows commands. These commands can be used by attackers in order to identify assets of value and coordinate lateral movement after compromising a machine.

event_16c04dbea06d8a6d.title: Suspected identity theft (pass-the-ticket)
event_16c04dbea06d8a6d.description: An actor took Julian Burke (IT director)'s Kerberos ticket from VNEVADO-Win10B and used it on VNEVADO-Win10V to access 4 resources.

event_1651286fcd7c2c21.title: User accessed link in ZAP-quarantined email
event_1651286fcd7c2c21.description: A user clicked on a link in an email that was quarantined by zero-hour auto purge (ZAP). This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Defender for Office 365 alert.

mapping.value: User accessed link in ZAP-quarantined email

event_0183065ef4d1eec6.title: Anomalous account lookups
event_0183065ef4d1eec6.description: An anomalous chain of attempts to look up user account information has been observed. An attacker might be gathering information about potential targets.

event_4d7908a2d1e814b6.title: 'Kekeo' malware was detected during lateral movement
event_4d7908a2d1e814b6.description: 'Kekeo' malware was detected on this device. An attacker might be attempting to move laterally to this device from another device on the network.

mapping.value: 'Kekeo' malware was detected during lateral movement

event_9d6ee67288e4d81c.title: User and IP address reconnaissance (SMB)
event_9d6ee67288e4d81c.description: Ethan Brooks (Account Executive) on VNEVADO-Win10V enumerated SMB sessions on VNEVADO-DC, retrieving recent IP addresses of 2 accounts.

event_b702753b4ae80a37.title: Microsoft Defender Antivirus tampering
event_b702753b4ae80a37.description:
An attempt to disable the Microsoft Defender Antivirus service was detected. This might an attempt to evade detection.

For more information, read the Antivirus tampering technique profile Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/9ce0ac71-e104-4e59-9d46-2a8e2cac5a1d/analystreport.

event_f4f380f21a699008.title: SID history injection
event_f4f380f21a699008.description: A Security IDentifcation (SID) history injection was detected on this device. SID history is an attribute that supports migration scenarios. Attackers typically use attack tools to change the SID history of an existing domain user to an SID with elevated privileges. With elevated privileges, the affected process might be able to access sensitive files, ensure persistence, and modify system settings.

event_7cb1156def220815.title: Suspicious process stopping services
event_7cb1156def220815.description: A process suspiciously stopped services running on the device. An attacker might stop a service to avoid detection, removal of malware, and recovery. This is often done in conjunction with data encryption or destruction, to render the device unusable.

event_2e0211f1eb7030cf.title: Suspicious account creation
event_2e0211f1eb7030cf.description: A new user account was created. A new user account can be created to establish a secondary of backup access to the device or services within the organization. An attacker might be attempting to maintain access to the device or organization.

event_aa3def90979dfa0f.title: Malicious URL was clicked on that device
event_aa3def90979dfa0f.description: Malicious URL was clicked on that device

mapping.value: Malicious URL was clicked on that device

event_b6d45ede7dcfcfe2.title: Attempt to hide use of dual-purpose tool
event_b6d45ede7dcfcfe2.description:
A known public tool, which could also be used for malicious reasons, was observed under an unexpected filename.
This might be an attempt to hide the usage of that tool for malicious purposes.

mapping.value: Attempt to hide use of dual-purpose tool

event_8c54af03667cb4fe.title: Suspicious System Hardware Discovery
event_8c54af03667cb4fe.description: A known tool or technique was used to gather information on this device. Attackers might be trying to gather information about the target device or network for later attacks.

event_90c457f34b6e760b.title: Suspicious service registration
event_90c457f34b6e760b.description: A system program was registered as a service. This can indicate malicious intent to establish persistence or gain system privileges.

event_d2f7bd1bb6b4b63c.title: Sensitive credential memory read
event_d2f7bd1bb6b4b63c.description: A process scanned or dumped memory from the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe).  Accessing this process memory allows the attacker to extract secrets such as authentication hashes or passwords.  A copy of this memory may be written to the file system and exfiltrated to extract these credentials offline.

event_897dc0fefedd6007.title: A process was injected with potentially malicious code
event_897dc0fefedd6007.description:
A process has injected code into another process, indicating suspicious code being run in the target process memory. Injection is often used to hide malicious code execution within a trusted process. 
As a result, the target process may exhibit abnormal behaviors such as opening a listening port or connecting to a command and control server.

mapping.value: A process was injected with potentially malicious code

event_0c1bdfc5dfa155bf.title: System executable renamed and launched
event_0c1bdfc5dfa155bf.description: A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched. Attackers might be attempting to use the executable to perform malicious activities, such as running malicious code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. By changing the path or file name of a system executable, attackers can avoid certain behavior-based detection technologies that rely on default paths and file names.

event_de68d32371281529.title: Ongoing hands-on-keyboard attack via Impacket toolkit
event_de68d32371281529.description:
Suspicious execution of a command via Impacket was observed on this device. This tool connects to other hosts to explore network shares and execute commands. Attackers might be attempting to move laterally across the network using this tool. This usage of Impacket has often been observed in hands-on-keyboard attacks, where ransomware and other payloads are installed on target devices.

Corresponding TA for this IOA: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/ff7e4fff-dde3-49be-9a06-7f63a490996d/analystreport

mapping.value: Ongoing hands-on-keyboard attack via Impacket toolkit

event_9650955f39328453.title: Suspected AD FS DKM key read
event_9650955f39328453.description: MB-DC1 read the DKM key of ADFS object id 4cac49d3-29d3-407e-8c9b-b7ebb21541b2

mapping.value: Suspected AD FS DKM key read

event_36e2c6b79fbb7a90.title: Internal phishing lexpaign
event_36e2c6b79fbb7a90.description: A user was observed to have sent phishing email from this device to recipients inside the organization. The user account might have been compromised in an attempt by an attacker to move laterally inside the organization. This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Defender for Office 365 alert.

event_17b802b122a0650d.title: A malicious PowerShell Cmdlet was invoked on the machine
event_17b802b122a0650d.description: A malicious PowerShell Cmdlet was invoked on the machine. The Cmdlet may be associated with credential theft, exploitation, network reconnaissance or code injection.

mapping.value: A malicious PowerShell Cmdlet was invoked on the machine

event_1f5d3930877fc307.title: Suspicious service creation
event_1f5d3930877fc307.description: gsmith created DDLOXJDSQSNGMUKKFUXQ in order to execute potentially malicious commands on MB-ADFS.

event_0a40a8be04243360.title: ADFS private key extraction attempt
event_0a40a8be04243360.description: A suspicious LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) query was launched. Attackers might be attempting to steal Active Directory Federation Service (ADFS) private keys or move laterally on the network.

event_be93e72b71d02289.title: Unusual addition of credentials to an OAuth app
event_be93e72b71d02289.description: The user Luciano Herrera (pwilson@niseko.alpineskihouse.co) performed an unusual addition of credentials to the application SimulandApp. This usage pattern may indicate that an attacker has compromised the app, and is using it to spread phishing, exfiltrate data, or to gain access to other accounts and devices. The user added a credential of type Password. A credential of type Password is added when an application is using a password to authenticate.

mapping.value: Unusual addition of credentials to an OAuth app

event_db3d3fd937047f56.title: Anonymous IP address
event_db3d3fd937047f56.description: Sign-in from an anonymous IP address (e.g. Tor browser, anonymizer VPNs)

event_d4ca9523d551b632.title: BEC financial fraud
event_d4ca9523d551b632.description: A suspicious inbox rule that hides incoming email messages was created in a risky Azure Active Directory session. An attacker might be attempting to conduct business email compromise (BEC), a form of financial fraud.

event_1fadc9aa9791105d.title: Suspicious emails sent by BEC-related user
event_1fadc9aa9791105d.description: Suspicious emails were sent by a possibly compromised user account related to an ongoing BEC (business email compromise) fraud attempt. This alert was triggered based on a previous BEC-related alert.

mapping.value: Suspicious emails sent by BEC-related user

event_3c487cd3846b07f5.title: Suspicious inbox manipulation rule
event_3c487cd3846b07f5.description: A user's inbox rules were manipulated in a suspicious manner. An attacker might have gained access to a user's inbox and is manipulating rules to delete or move messages or folders to exfiltrate data from your organization.

event_50c0dbb2b32435fb.title: Account compromised following a password-spray attack
event_50c0dbb2b32435fb.description: A user was signed in from an unusual location and browser during a password spray attack. An attacker might have compromised the user account for unauthorized access to the network. We recommend prompt investigation to mitigate potential security risks.

mapping.value: Account compromised following a password-spray attack

event_f8901a6fd8091ef7.title: Malicious IP address
event_f8901a6fd8091ef7.description: Sign-in from an IP address known to be malicious during or around the time of sign-in

event_35755b968cf46296.title: Suspicious SAP authentication
event_35755b968cf46296.description: A user account with a risky sign-in alert in Microsoft Entra ID signed in to SAP, the enterprise application software. An attacker might have taken control of a user account to search through SAP with the intention of recording or modifying sensitive financial information. The gathered information might be used for later stages in the attack, such as phishing or social engineering. This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Entra ID alert.

event_0adffd181e3df166.title: Possible BEC financial fraud
event_0adffd181e3df166.description: Suspicious events with business email compromise (BEC) characteristics were observed. An attacker might be attempting to conduct a Fraud attack against your organization.

event_2efa642a3230ffa1.title: BEC-related user signed in to SAP
event_2efa642a3230ffa1.description: A user involved in a business email compromise-related alert also signed in to SAP in a suspicious manner. An attacker might have taken control of a user account to search through SAP with the intention of recording or modifying sensitive financial information. The gathered information might be used for later stages in the attack, such as phishing or social engineering. This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Defender XDR alert.

mapping.value: BEC-related user signed in to SAP

event_b9bba10cab40ba3c.title: Suspicious credential dump from NTDS.dit
event_b9bba10cab40ba3c.description: Attackers dump NTDS.dit in order to obtain user's credentials which are stored in the domain controller.

event_40a629dee3b57387.title: Suspicious Azure Resource Management activities by a risky user
event_40a629dee3b57387.description: Suspicious cloud Azure Resource Management (ARM) activities were performed by a user account that signed in to a risky session. This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Defender for Cloud alert related to ARM and Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk scores.

mapping.value: Suspicious Azure Resource Management activities by a risky user

event_edb58aa6f55700b4.title: Azure Resource Manager operation from suspicious proxy IP address
event_edb58aa6f55700b4.description: Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager detected a resource management operation from an IP address that is associated with proxy services, such as TOR. While this behavior can be legitimate, it's often seen in malicious activities, when threat actors try to hide their source IP.

mapping.value: Azure Resource Manager operation from suspicious proxy IP address

event_714577085071e2dd.title: Malicious Url detected in Proxy logs
event_714577085071e2dd.description: Connection from 231.60.52.209 - vnevado-win11h.vnevado.alpineskihouse.co to login.micro.demo.antoinetest.ovh has been seen on the proxy, please check on the computer what happened

mapping.value: Malicious Url detected in Proxy logs

event_a4769c04bb1f4cab.title: User accessed a link in an email subsequently quarantined by ZAP
event_a4769c04bb1f4cab.description: A user clicked on a link in an email that was later quarantined by zero-hour auto purge (ZAP). This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Defender for Office 365 alert.

mapping.value: User accessed a link in an email subsequently quarantined by ZAP

event_3eea7a0693f3a822.title: Ntdsutil collecting Active Directory information
event_3eea7a0693f3a822.description: Attackers might be using Ntdsutil to gather information for persistence or to move laterally in a network or organization. Ntdsutil is a command line tool that provides management facilities for Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) and Active Directory Lightweight Directory Services (AD LDS). It was launched to maintain the database of AD DS.
